criterion.described: The Criterion Bar, Piccadilly, 1881, early afternoon: a long mahogany counter with a brass foot-rail under a great gilt-framed mirror, gasoliers burning yellow through tobacco haze, marble pillars, bottles ranked on glass shelves, a tiled floor; drinkers stand two deep at the near end by the doors and thin to an empty stretch of counter at the far end under the mirror; behind the counter hangs the gilt mirror, which gives back the men's backs and the gasoliers; warm gaslight indoors, with the wet grey daylight of the street lying beyond the doors.
criterion.landmark: the great gilt-framed mirror behind the counter
criterion.route: from the crowded doors at the counter's near end, along the counter, to its quieter far end under the mirror
criterion.geometry: The counter is one straight run of mahogany crossing the frame, the brass foot-rail along its foot nearest the camera at the bottom of frame. The great gilt-framed mirror is fixed flat to the wall BEHIND the counter, above the ranked bottles, and it gives back the backs of the men standing at the counter and the gasoliers above them. The wall behind the counter is panelling and shelved bottles from one edge of frame to the other. In every panel the camera stands on the drinkers' side of the counter and keeps to that side, so the bottles and the mirror are always beyond the men, and the men move along the counter from the LEFT edge of frame toward the RIGHT edge, the crowded doors behind them at the LEFT.
criterion.crowd: eight or nine men in top hats and bowlers standing two deep at the counter, a white-aproned barman drawing a cork, a waiter crossing left to right with a tray

cab.described: A black two-wheeled hansom cab, 1881, on wet cobbled London streets under a grey afternoon sky: a bay horse in the shafts, two tall spoked wheels, a folding hood, the cabman on his high seat up behind the hood, a brass side-lamp at each front corner; inside, one buttoned leather seat for two passengers side by side under the low hood, the hood closing behind and above them, the small rain-streaked front glass and the leather apron ahead of them, the horse's back beyond the glass; shopfronts and gas lamps lit early sliding past.
cab.landmark: the brass side-lamp on the cab's near front corner
cab.route: from the Criterion's kerb in Piccadilly through the wet streets to the hospital gateway
cab.geometry: This vehicle is a hansom cab and it is built like this. ONE pair of tall spoked wheels, one wheel on each side of the body, their axle passing UNDER THE MIDDLE of the passenger box, so the wheels stand beside the passengers at their shoulder. The bay horse stands in the two long shafts that run forward from the body: the gap from the front rim of the near wheel to the horse's hind hooves is two thirds of one wheel's width of open cobble, crossed high up by the black underside of those two shafts, and the whole rig from the horse's nose to the back of the driver's high seat measures three times its own height. The driver sits high at the BACK of the roof, above and behind the passengers' heads, and the reins run forward over the roof to the horse. One brass side-lamp is mounted on each front corner of the body at the passengers' shoulder height, so one of them burns on the flank the camera sees in every exterior panel. The two passengers sit side by side facing FORWARD, toward the horse, the folding hood closing behind and above their heads as one blank sheet of black leather, the small rain-streaked front glass and the leather apron ahead of their knees, the horse's back and the reins beyond that glass. In every exterior panel the camera stands on the pavement on the near side of the street and keeps to that pavement: the cab travels from the LEFT edge of frame toward the RIGHT edge, horse leading, so the horse is nearer the RIGHT edge, the driver nearer the LEFT edge, and the water thrown by the wheels flies backward toward the LEFT edge.
cab.crowd: four pedestrians under umbrellas on the far pavement, a boy with a broom at the crossing, a second cab waiting at the kerb beyond

gateway.described: The street front of Saint Bartholomew's Hospital, 1881: a stone gateway arch onto the wet cobbled street, iron gates open, worn stone steps beyond the arch up to a small side-door in soot-dark brick, a pavement with iron railings along the hospital wall running to a corner, gas lamps on iron posts unlit, fog thinning, rain just stopped; the arrival panels stand in the flat grey daylight of that wet early afternoon and the departure panels stand later the same day, with one band of low amber sun along the top course of the wall and the pavement flags in blue shade.
gateway.landmark: the stone arch of the gateway
gateway.route: from the kerb under the gateway arch and its steps, along the pavement past the iron railings, to the corner where a cab waits
gateway.geometry: The gateway is ONE round stone arch with its iron gates standing open, set in a soot-dark brick wall, and it is the one opening in that wall in frame. Through the arch and deeper into the picture, worn stone steps rise to one small side-door: the steps stand BEHIND the arch, farther from the camera, and they read smaller than it. The iron railings run from the arch along the pavement toward the corner, shrinking as they go, and the corner closes the far end of the pavement. In every panel the camera keeps to the street side of the railings, so the hospital wall is always beyond the people and the kerb is always nearest the camera.
gateway.crowd: three men in dark coats talking under the arch, a porter wheeling a barrow along the railings, a woman with a basket on the far pavement
gateway.landmark_size: is half the height of the frame

corridor.described: A long stone corridor inside Saint Bartholomew's Hospital, 1881: flagstone floor worn hollow, whitewashed walls stained with damp, dun-coloured doors, tall barred windows on one side throwing cold grey daylight in bars across the floor, unlit gas brackets, an open doorway to a dissecting room with a slab under a high window, and at the far end a low arched passage.
corridor.landmark: the pale barred window showing inside the low arched passage at the far end of the corridor
corridor.route: from the corridor's near end, past the barred windows and the dissecting-room doorway, to the low arched passage at its far end
corridor.geometry: The corridor is one straight run away from the camera. The flagstone floor holds the bottom of frame; the tall barred windows stand in a row down ONE side of it and lay their bars of cold daylight across the floor toward the opposite wall; the low arched passage closes the far end at the CENTRE of the frame, small and pale, and grows larger the farther along the corridor the camera stands. The dissecting-room doorway is one opening in the wall opposite the windows, halfway along. In every panel the camera keeps the tall barred windows on the RIGHT side of frame, and it stands at its own height and its own distance along the corridor in each panel.
corridor.crowd: a porter in a leather apron carrying a covered tray away down the corridor, two students in black coats standing at a doorway

lab.described: The chemical laboratory of Saint Bartholomew's Hospital, 1881, seen from its door: a lofty chamber lined with countless bottles, broad low tables scattered with retorts, test-tubes and little Bunsen lamps with blue flickering flames, a tall arched window centred at the far end and under it Holmes's own working table with a wooden stool, cold daylight mixed with the blue of the flames; the bench setup is this same room seen from its middle toward that window.
lab.landmark: the tall window at the far end of the laboratory
lab.route: from the laboratory doorway, between the long benches, to the middle of the room facing the far window
lab.geometry: The laboratory is one lofty room seen down its length. The long low benches run away from the camera on both sides, crowded with retorts, test-tubes and little Bunsen lamps with blue flames; the bottle-lined shelves stand along both side walls from the door to the far end; and the tall arched window closes that far end at the CENTRE of the frame, with Holmes's own working table and its wooden stool under it. The window grows larger the farther into the room the camera stands. In every panel the camera keeps to the aisle between the benches, so the long benches are at both edges of frame; the panels that look down the room hold the tall arched window at the CENTRE of frame, and the two panels that look back up the aisle from the far end hold the open laboratory door small and pale behind the man they face.
lab.crowd: one student in shirtsleeves at a far bench with his back turned, working

bench.described: Holmes's own working table under the tall arched window of the chemical laboratory, 1881: the SAME room as the lab setup, seen from the middle of the room toward its far window, the reverse angle of the lab, so the far arched window fills the top of frame and the same bottle-lined shelves stand either side, and the frame holds that one window alone; a broad low bench crowded with retorts and a rack of test-tubes, a litre glass vessel of clear water, a Bunsen lamp's blue flame, white crystals in a dish, an open notebook and pen, two high three-legged stools, acid stains on the wood; cold window light with the blue of the flame.
bench.landmark: the Bunsen lamp's blue flame on the bench
bench.route: from the near end of Holmes's bench, along it under the window, to its far end and the way back toward the door
bench.geometry: The bench is the SAME laboratory turned round: the camera stands in the middle of the room and looks at Holmes's own working table under the tall arched window, so the window fills the TOP of the frame, the bottle-lined shelves stand at both side edges, and the table crosses the BOTTOM of the frame with its litre vessel, its pipette and its bodkin on it. That window is the one opening in the wall behind the table and the one source of light, and it stands larger the nearer the camera stands to the table: whole and pale across the TOP of frame from the room's side of the bench, small and high at the CENTRE of the top of frame from the doorway at the near end of the room. In the panels drawn from the room's side of the table Holmes stands beyond it with the litre vessel nearest the camera; the one panel drawn close behind Holmes's own left shoulder holds that shoulder in the LEFT third of frame with the vessel beyond his hands.
bench.crowd: one student in shirtsleeves at a far bench with his back turned, working
bench.landmark_size: is the height of a finger

shots.frame: Medium close-up at the crowded near end of the Criterion counter: Stamford, dark hair, round clean-shaven face, in a black frock coat, his hand just lifted from a tweed shoulder, facing Watson's tweed back at the frame edge; drinkers soft behind; yellow gaslight, the gilt mirror behind the counter reflecting their backs; Stamford's mouth is closed, the line on his lips.
shots.motion: Static shot; Stamford speaks the line to the man in front of him; over the first 2 seconds Watson turns his whole body round from the counter to face Stamford, his tweed shoulder and profile filling the left of frame; Stamford's hand rises open to chest height as he speaks and drops back to his side by 5 seconds.
shots.camera: on the drinkers' side of the counter at its crowded near end, at standing eye height, a normal lens, turned along the mahogany toward the quieter far end, so Watson's brown tweed back and the back of his dark head fill the LEFT edge nearest the camera and out of focus, Stamford stands beyond him through the right two-thirds of the frame, and the ranked bottles, the burning gasoliers and the gilt mirror lie small and soft on the wall beyond them both
shots.at_rest: Stamford's open hand hangs in the air a few inches above the brown tweed shoulder, the fingers spread and the arm at rest; his lips are together and his eyebrows level; Watson's back stays square to the mahogany with both shoulders level and the back of his head toward the camera, the brown bowler hanging low in his left hand at his side; along the counter the white-aproned barman stands with his corkscrew half-turned into a bottle and the waiter halts with his tray held level at shoulder height.
shots.crowd: the white-aproned barman with his corkscrew half-turned into a bottle and a waiter halted with his tray level at shoulder height

shots.frame: Close on Watson turned from the counter near its crowded end, bareheaded, dark hair swept back, gaunt sunburnt face, thin moustache, mouth closed, the brown bowler in the hand on the right of frame held against his chest; Stamford's black shoulder at the left edge; gaslight, drinkers blurred behind.
shots.motion: Static shot; Watson turns the brown bowler a half turn against his chest in his left hand over the first 2 seconds; his head turns from Stamford down to the hat and back up to Stamford by 3 seconds; his lips stay closed.

cuts.frame: Insert at the brass foot-rail, same place at the counter: Watson's bare sunburnt hand on the silver ball knob of his black stick, the frayed tweed cuff above it, a wine glass beside it on the mahogany; the only hand in frame.
cuts.motion: Static shot; the hand leaves the knob, closes round the wine glass and lifts it up out of the top of frame over 2 seconds; by 3.5 seconds the silver knob stands alone on the rail and the hand comes back down onto it.
cuts.camera: out on the drinkers' side of the counter, set at the height of the hand on the stick's knob and a pace back from the panelled counter front, a close-focus lens square to that front, so the polished mahogany edge of the counter top and the foot of a wine glass stand along the TOP of frame, the bare sunburnt hand and the silver ball knob fill the CENTRE, the dark panelled counter front stands behind them from edge to edge, the brass foot-rail runs as a bright horizontal line low in the frame, and the stick's iron ferrule and the tiled floor hold the bottom edge
cuts.at_rest: the fingers are fully closed round the silver ball knob with the knuckles flat, the black stick standing plumb beneath them and its ferrule set square on the tiled floor; the wine glass stands on its own foot on the mahogany a hand's width to the right, an inch of dark red in it, the surface flat and level; the frayed tweed cuff lies against the back of the hand; the reflections in the polished wood hold steady.

shots.camera: one step farther along the counter on the drinkers' side, square to Watson at his own eye height, a long lens, so his head and shoulders fill the frame and the ranked bottles, the gasoliers and the gilt mirror behind the counter go soft far beyond him
shots.at_rest: the brown bowler rests flat against Watson's chest in his left hand, which is on the right of frame, both edges of its brim level and his fingers closed on the crown; his head is level, his eyes are on Stamford, his mouth is closed and his jaw is set; his other hand, his bare sunburnt right, is closed round the silver ball knob of the black stick at the counter's rail nearest the camera; behind him at the rail a drinker holds a folded newspaper open in both hands and reads it.
shots.crowd: one drinker at the brass rail holding a folded newspaper open in both hands and reading it

shots.frame: Medium two-shot a few steps further along the counter: Stamford at right, dark hair, round clean-shaven face, black frock coat, and Watson at left facing him over two glasses, bareheaded, the bowler in his far hand at his side, the black stick's silver knob under his bare sunburnt hand nearer the camera at the counter's rail, mouths closed; the gilt mirror behind them showing their own backs.
shots.motion: Static shot; Stamford drinks from the raised glass and sets it down on the counter by 2 seconds; Watson picks up his own glass from the counter and drinks over the last 2 seconds; Stamford's head turns to look Watson up and down, from his face to his stick and back, over the whole shot.

cuts.frame: Close on Stamford, same place at the counter, dark hair, round clean-shaven face, his glass standing on the mahogany at the bottom of frame with his hand flat on the wood beside it, an odd measuring look along Watson's coat, mouth closed; gaslight on one side of his face, the gilt mirror behind him.
cuts.motion: Static shot; Stamford lifts the glass from the counter to his lips and drinks over the first 2 seconds; then his head turns away from Watson toward the doors and back to him by 4 seconds.
cuts.camera: close in at the quieter end of the counter, still on the drinkers' side, set low at chest height and looking up under Stamford's chin, a long lens, so his face fills the upper two-thirds of the frame and the carved gilt frame of the great mirror runs down the LEFT edge behind his shoulder with one lit gasolier burning beside it
cuts.at_rest: Stamford's wine glass stands on the mahogany at the bottom of frame in its own wet ring with an inch of dark red in it, his fingers spread flat on the wood beside it and that arm at rest; his eyes hold their sideways measuring look along Watson's coat and his mouth is closed; his far shoulder is squared and settled, his other hand down out of frame; behind him a drinker leans on the brass rail with both elbows and the gasolier burns steady.
cuts.crowd: one drinker leaning on the brass rail with both elbows under a gasolier burning steady

shots.camera: a few steps farther along the counter at its quieter end, standing back on the drinkers' side at chest height, a normal lens, square to the mahogany, so Watson stands in the LEFT third of frame in three-quarter profile facing right, Stamford stands in the RIGHT third facing him, both men on the camera's own side of the counter with the ranked bottles and the gilt mirror on the wall beyond them and the brass foot-rail crossing the bottom of frame
shots.at_rest: both wine glasses stand on the mahogany between the two men, each on its own foot with an inch of dark red in it, and both men's hands rest away from them; Stamford's right hand lies flat and open on the counter beside his glass and his eyes are level on Watson's face; Watson's bare sunburnt right hand is closed on the silver ball knob of the black stick at the counter's rail nearest the camera, the brown bowler in his far left hand at his side with its brim level; both mouths are closed; behind them the barman stands with a bottle tilted over a fresh glass and the waiter waits at the counter's end with his tray held level.
shots.end: The same stretch of mahogany in the same yellow gaslight, a moment later: Watson's wine glass is up at his mouth in his bare sunburnt right hand, his chin lifted and his eyes above the rim on Stamford; the black walking stick leans against the panelled counter front with its silver ball knob against the mahogany's edge and its ferrule on the tiled floor; the brown bowler stays in his far left hand at his side; Stamford's glass stands back on the counter in a wet ring, lower by an inch, his fingers spread flat on the wood beside it, his head come down and his eyes travelling along Watson's coat to the black stick at the rail; the great gilt-framed mirror on the wall beyond them holds both men's backs and the gasoliers above them; the barman draws the cork clear of the bottle neck and pours, and the waiter has carried his tray to the right edge of frame.
shots.changed: Watson's glass has risen to his mouth in the LEFT third of frame, a hand tall.
shots.crowd: the white-aproned barman tilting a bottle over a fresh glass and a waiter waiting at the counter's end with his tray held level

shots.frame: Wide exterior, a wet cobbled street just off Piccadilly under a grey afternoon sky: a black two-wheeled hansom entering from the left at a trot, a bay horse in the shafts, the cabman up on his high seat behind the folding hood, the brass side-lamp at the corner, two hatted figures side by side under the hood; shopfronts, gas lamps lit early.
shots.motion: Static shot; the hansom enters at the left edge of frame and travels the whole width of the street at a trot, the horse advancing along the cobbles and the wheels turning, and leaves at the right edge of frame by 3.5 seconds; its wheels throw water from a puddle as it passes the centre.

cuts.frame: Insert low beside the moving hansom, still in the same street: the tall spoked wheel and the brass side-lamp, the horse's hind legs ahead of the wheel, rain-wet cobbles blurring beneath, spray flying.
cuts.motion: Tracking beside the hansom at the horse's trot for the whole shot; the wheel turns through full revolutions and the cobbles and shopfronts stream past behind it; the hooves strike and spray flies at every stride.
cuts.camera: down on the wet cobbles at the near kerb, the lens at the height of the near wheel's hub, a forearm's length above the stones, a normal lens held square to the cab's flank so the far pavement and its shopfronts lie flat along the top of frame and the street runs out of frame at both the LEFT and the RIGHT edge, the one tall wheel filling the LEFT half of frame from the bottom edge to two thirds of the way up it
cuts.at_rest: The one tall spoked wheel of this near flank fills the LEFT half of frame, its twelve spokes at rest, a chip in its iron tyre standing at the very top of the rim, its hub a bright boss at the middle of that half and its bottom rim standing in the shallow water at the bottom edge of frame. The black lower body panel of the cab fills the whole space above and behind the wheel's upper arc and runs back to the bottom LEFT corner, so this one wheel is the whole running gear on this flank, and the front corner of that body stands at the TOP CENTRE of frame with the brass side-lamp of this near flank burning on it at the passengers' shoulder height. Behind the wheel's lower arc the wet cobbles run flat across frame to the far kerb. From the front rim of the wheel to the RIGHT edge of frame lie two thirds of a wheel's width of open wet cobble, crossed high up by the two long black shafts, which run out of frame at the RIGHT edge; at that RIGHT edge the bay horse's near hind leg stands with the hoof flat on the stones and the hock at the height of the wheel's hub. One sheet of water stands heaped and unbroken at the foot of the wheel where the tyre sits in a puddle. Along the top of frame beyond the shafts a lit shopfront window and its doorway stand square and whole and out of focus, with two pedestrians under one umbrella halted at that doorway.
cuts.end: The same low place on the cobbles at the near kerb, the same lens square to the cab's flank, the same wheel at the same size in the LEFT half of frame and the same grey light, one moment later: the chip in the iron tyre has travelled half a turn from the top of the rim down to the cobbles at the bottom edge of frame and the spokes are drawn into a blur of turning, the hub bright at the middle of that half. The heaped sheet of water has left the stones and hangs behind the wheel as a broad fan flying toward the LEFT edge of frame, and the puddle it came out of lies flat and shallow at the bottom LEFT corner. Along the top of frame beyond the shafts, the lit shopfront window and its doorway have travelled out past the LEFT edge and the foot of an iron lamp post and a butcher's lit window stand square in the top RIGHT of frame in their place, a woman with a basket walking past that window. At the RIGHT edge the bay horse's near hind hoof is up at the top of its stride with the fetlock folded and the off hind hoof flat on the stones. The two thirds of a wheel's width of open cobble between the wheel and the horse holds its width, the two black shafts hold their height across it, and the brass side-lamp burns at the TOP CENTRE as it did.
cuts.changed: The chip in the tyre has turned down to the BOTTOM edge of frame, a thumbnail wide.

shots.camera: on the near pavement on this side of the street, at the head height of a standing man, a wide lens held square across to the far kerb so the shopfronts run flat along the whole width of frame behind the cab, the whole vehicle in frame from the horse's nose to the back of the driver's high seat, standing a sixth of the height of the frame and half of its width, with a full vehicle's length of open wet cobble between the horse's nose and the RIGHT edge of frame; the wet cobbles fill the bottom third of frame, the lit shopfront windows and the first-floor brick fill the top half, and the cab stands in the band between them
shots.at_rest: The hansom stands halted at the LEFT of frame with its whole length inside the picture: the back of the driver's high seat a hand's breadth inside the LEFT edge, the black passenger box and its one near wheel filling the left quarter of frame, the two long shafts crossing the next quarter, and the bay horse's nose standing at the middle of frame with a full vehicle's length of open wet cobble between that nose and the RIGHT edge. It runs on one tall spoked wheel on this near flank and one matching wheel on the far flank, those two the whole of its running gear, their single axle crossing under the middle of the passenger box, so the near wheel's top rim stands level with the passengers' shoulders and its hub level with their hip, and the black body is slung low between the wheels with its floor a hand's breadth above the cobbles. The black lower body panel fills the whole space behind the wheel's upper arc and runs back from it to the tail of the cab. The two passengers sit side by side on the one seat under the folding hood with their faces along the street toward the RIGHT edge of frame, the black folding doors closed across their knees, their two hatted heads together in the middle of the body and the blank black leather of the hood closing behind and above them. The cabman sits on his high seat at the BACK of the roof, above and behind those two heads, his own hat the highest thing in the picture, and his reins run forward over the roof and down to the bay horse's bit. The bay horse stands square in the two long shafts with all four hooves flat on the cobbles and its head toward the RIGHT edge, and the space between the front rim of the near wheel and the horse's hind hooves is two thirds of a wheel's width of open wet cobble crossed high up by the two black shafts alone. The brass side-lamp burns at the front corner of the body at the passengers' shoulder height, the size of a thumbnail. A puddle lies whole and flat as a mirror in the middle of the street at the centre of frame. Along the far pavement four pedestrians walk under umbrellas about their own errands, a boy with a broom stands at the crossing with both hands on the handle, and a second hansom waits at the far kerb toward the RIGHT edge with its horse's head down.
shots.end: The same stretch of street from the same place on the near pavement, the same normal lens square to the far kerb, the same grey afternoon light and the same shopfronts flat along the whole width of frame. The hansom now stands at the RIGHT of frame: the bay horse's head and shoulders have passed out through the RIGHT edge, its hind quarters and the two long shafts fill the right third of frame, the one tall near wheel stands at the right of centre with its spokes drawn into a blur by the turn, the black body and the two hatted passengers behind their closed folding doors ride at the right of centre with the brass side-lamp burning at the body's front corner, and the cabman keeps his high seat at the BACK of the roof with the reins running forward over it. The puddle at the centre of frame is burst into one white sheet of water thrown back toward the LEFT edge, hanging over the cobbles at the height of the wheel hub, and the cobbles the cab has crossed lie wet and open from the LEFT edge to the middle of frame. The iron lamp post on the near kerb, the lit shopfront windows, the far kerb, the gas lamps lit early and the first-floor brick hold their own places and their own sizes. The boy with the broom has stepped back onto the kerb with the broom head lifted off the stones, two of the four pedestrians under umbrellas have turned their heads after the cab, and the second hansom waits at the far kerb where it stood.
shots.changed: The hansom has crossed to the RIGHT of frame, still a sixth of the frame's height.
shots.crowd: four pedestrians under umbrellas on the far pavement about their own errands, a boy at the crossing with both hands on his broom handle, and a second hansom waiting at the far kerb

shots.frame: Close inside the hansom under the low hood, midway to the hospital: Watson in his brown bowler, gaunt sunburnt face, thin moustache, mouth closed, eyes on the small rain-streaked front glass ahead of him with the horse's back beyond it; the hood closing behind and above his head; Stamford's black shoulder and round clean-shaven face at the right edge, soft; grey light.
shots.motion: Static shot inside the moving cab; the shopfronts and gas lamps slide past the side window behind him for the whole shot; a jolt at 1 second lifts Watson off the seat and drops him back; his head turns from the front glass to the side window and back to the glass by 3 seconds.

cuts.frame: Insert inside the hansom, same seat: Watson's bare sunburnt hand gripping the silver ball knob of the black stick planted between his knees, the tweed cuff frayed, the cab floor wet; the only hand in frame.
cuts.motion: Static shot inside the moving cab; the wet street slides past at the top of frame for the whole shot; a jolt at 1 second knocks the stick sideways and the hand catches it and plants it upright again by 2 seconds; the hand presses the ferrule down onto the wet floor by 3 seconds.
cuts.camera: inside the passenger box, set low over the wet floorboards a forearm's length from Watson's knees and level with his hands, a close-focus lens looking down the length of the black walking stick, the hand and the silver ball knob filling the middle of frame at the height of a fist, the frayed tweed cuff at the top of frame and the iron ferrule and the wet floorboards at the bottom edge
cuts.at_rest: The bare sunburnt right hand is closed over the silver ball knob with the thumb laid across the fingers and the knuckles standing up, the wrist straight, and the black stick stands plumb from that knob down through the middle of frame to its iron ferrule, which is set square on the wet floorboards between both boots. The frayed brown tweed cuff and a white shirt cuff lie along the back of that wrist at the top of frame. The dark trouser knees stand at either side of the stick, the black folding doors closed across them at the top RIGHT of frame, and the floorboards carry a thin film of rainwater with the street's grey light lying flat along it. The silver ball holds one small bright window of daylight on its crown, and the reflections in the wet boards hold steady.

shots.camera: inside the passenger box at its front LEFT corner just within the folding doors, set low at the men's chest height so the lens looks up at Watson's face, a portrait lens turned back across the seat, so Watson's head and shoulders fill the LEFT two thirds of frame in three-quarter face seen slightly from below, the blank black leather of the folding hood closes across the whole top of frame behind his head, and Stamford's black shoulder stands soft and cropped at the RIGHT edge
shots.at_rest: Watson sits square on the buttoned leather seat with his back against it and both shoulders level, the brown bowler square on his head, his gaunt sunburnt face and thin waxed moustache turned a little past the camera toward the small rain-streaked front glass with the bay horse's back beyond it, his lips together and his eyes steady. The black folding doors lie closed across both men's knees along the bottom of frame, his bare sunburnt right hand resting flat on the top of them and the silver ball knob of the black stick standing up under his other hand at the bottom LEFT corner. At the RIGHT edge Stamford sits back with both hands down and his round face toward the front of the cab. Through the rain-streaked side glass at the LEFT edge of frame the lit window of a shopfront stands whole and square and out of focus with one iron lamp post at the edge of it, and on the pavement past that glass a man in a dark coat walks under an umbrella and a woman with a basket stands at a doorway. The flat grey afternoon light lies along both faces and the black leather of the hood holds its own shadow.
shots.crowd: one man in a dark coat under an umbrella on the pavement past the side glass and a woman with a basket at a doorway

shots.frame: Medium close from the side inside the hansom, midway to the hospital: Watson in profile, brown bowler on, face to the side window, mouth closed, the arm nearer the camera held stiff against his tweed coat; beyond him at the right edge Stamford's black shoulder and round clean-shaven face, soft; the hood above and behind them, grey light.
shots.motion: Static shot inside the moving cab; the street and shopfronts stream past the side window behind Watson's profile for the whole shot; a jolt at 1 second throws him toward the camera and his far hand comes up and grips the stick's knob to steady him by 2 seconds; the stiff arm nearer the camera hangs at his side throughout.

cuts.frame: Insert from the passengers' seat inside the hansom, midway to the hospital: the small rain-streaked front glass and the leather apron below it, the bay horse's back and the reins beyond the glass, the wet street and shopfronts sliding toward the camera; the horse and the street fill the frame.
cuts.motion: Static shot from the passengers' seat; the horse trots ahead and the wet street, shopfronts and gas lamps rush toward the camera and pass out of both edges of frame for the whole shot; rain runs down the glass; the horse's back rises and falls at every stride.
cuts.camera: from the passengers' own place on the seat, set at their eye height midway between the two men and turned forward along the street, a wide lens, the leather apron and the black frame of the small rain-streaked front glass across the bottom of frame, the bay horse's rump and back filling the lower middle of frame and the wet street running away to a vanishing point at the centre
cuts.at_rest: The bay horse stands square in the shafts with its rump and back filling the lower middle of frame, its four hooves flat on the cobbles, its ears up and its mane lying over, and the two reins run from the top corners of the black apron forward along its flanks to the bit, the two long shafts running forward past those flanks. The rain stands on the front glass in beads with one run of water lying down the pane. Past the horse the wet cobbled street runs away between two rows of shopfronts to a vanishing point at the centre of frame, an iron lamp post standing tall at the LEFT of that street with its glass lit early and a second lamp post standing small and far at the RIGHT, and the grey sky lies between the roofs along the top of frame. On the pavement at the LEFT two men in dark coats walk under umbrellas, a boy with a broom stands at the crossing far down the street at the RIGHT, and a second cab waits small and far at the RIGHT kerb.
cuts.end: The same place on the seat at the same eye height, the same wide lens forward along the street, the same beaded rain on the front glass and the same flat grey light, one moment later: the bay horse's back has risen, its off hind leg is up under it at the top of the stride and its near forehoof reaches forward above the cobbles, its head lifted and both reins drawn straighter from the top corners of the black apron. The iron lamp post that stood small and far at the RIGHT of the street now stands tall at the RIGHT edge of frame with its lit glass at the height of the horse's ears, the shopfronts at both sides stand larger and wider with their lit windows spread to both edges of frame, and the crossing where the boy stood with his broom lies at the bottom RIGHT of frame with the boy himself up on the kerb and his broom on his shoulder. A fresh stretch of wet cobbled street runs away to the vanishing point at the centre with a brewer's dray standing far off at the LEFT kerb. One fresh run of rainwater lies down the front glass.
cuts.changed: The lamp post has grown to the RIGHT edge of frame, as tall as the horse's ears.

shots.camera: inside the passenger box hard against its LEFT side glass, at the height of the men's faces, a portrait lens turned straight across the box, so Watson's head stands in strict profile through the middle of frame facing the LEFT edge and the RAIN-STREAKED RIGHT-HAND SIDE GLASS fills the whole background behind his face with the grey street sliding past beyond it, the folding hood a dark band along the top edge alone
shots.at_rest: Watson sits with his spine against the buttoned leather and his face turned full to the side glass at the LEFT edge, the brown bowler square on his head, his lips together and his eyes on the street; the arm nearer the camera hangs stiff along his brown tweed coat with that shoulder dropped low, and his far hand lies flat on his thigh a hand's breadth from the silver ball knob of the black stick, which stands plumb between his knees at the bottom of frame with its ferrule on the wet floorboards. Through the side glass at the LEFT edge the lit windows of a chemist's shopfront stand whole and square and out of focus behind the run of rain on the pane, one iron lamp post standing up through the middle of that glass, and a man under an umbrella walks the pavement past it. At the RIGHT edge Stamford sits still with his round clean-shaven face toward the front of the cab and both hands down on the closed black folding door. The blank black leather of the folding hood closes across the top of frame.
shots.crowd: one man under an umbrella on the pavement past the lit windows of a chemist's shopfront

shots.frame: Medium close inside the hansom, nearing the hospital: Stamford in strict profile, dark hair, round clean-shaven face, black frock coat, looking out the side past the brass lamp, mouth closed; Watson's tweed shoulder and bowler brim nearer the camera; the hood above them, grey light, the street sliding past.
shots.motion: Static shot inside the moving cab; the shopfronts slide past the side window beyond Stamford for the whole shot; he raises his arm and points out past the brass lamp at something in the street, the arm fully extended by 1.5 seconds, and lowers it by 3 seconds; his head follows the thing he pointed at back past the lamp.

cuts.frame: Close on Watson in the hansom, same seat, brown bowler on, mouth closed, turned to watch Stamford's averted round face and black shoulder at the right edge of frame, soft; grey light through the small front glass.
cuts.motion: Static shot inside the moving cab; the street slides past the front glass behind him for the whole shot; Watson turns his whole head from Stamford at the right edge round to the front glass over 1.5 seconds; a jolt at 2 seconds rocks him sideways against the seat and he rights himself by 3 seconds.
cuts.camera: inside the passenger box at its front right corner, set low at the height of the closed folding doors and looking up at Watson from below his chin, a portrait lens, so his jaw, the underside of the bowler brim and the black leather of the hood fill the upper LEFT two thirds of frame, the silver ball knob of the black stick stands large in the BOTTOM LEFT corner nearest the camera, and Stamford's black shoulder and averted round face stand soft at the RIGHT edge
cuts.at_rest: Watson sits with his back on the buttoned leather and his whole head turned to the RIGHT edge of frame toward Stamford's averted round face, the brown bowler square on his head, his lips together, his eyes level and steady under the brim and his thin waxed moustache along his lip. His bare sunburnt right hand is closed on the silver ball knob of the black stick at the bottom of frame with the stick plumb between his knees, and his other hand lies flat on the closed black folding door. The grey daylight off the small front glass lies along one side of his face and leaves the other side in the shadow of the hood. At the RIGHT edge Stamford's black shoulder and the round of his face are held toward the street and stand out of focus. In the narrow strip of side glass at the LEFT edge a lit window and the tops of iron railings stand soft and grey, with one man in a dark coat on the pavement past them.
cuts.crowd: one man in a dark coat on the pavement beyond the iron railings in the side glass

shots.camera: on the seat itself between the two men, at their own shoulder height, a portrait lens turned to the left-hand side of the box, so Watson's brown tweed shoulder and the curve of his bowler brim stand large, near and soft across the whole LEFT edge closest to the lens, Stamford's head and shoulders stand sharp in strict profile through the middle of frame facing the RIGHT edge, and the lit brass side-lamp burns behind him at the RIGHT edge at his shoulder height
shots.at_rest: Stamford sits back on the buttoned leather with both shoulders down and level, his round clean-shaven face in strict profile to the RIGHT edge, his lips together and his small bright eyes on the street past the lamp; his near hand lies flat on his knee and his far hand rests on the top of the closed black folding door at the bottom RIGHT of frame with that elbow folded at his side, and his black frock coat and grey waistcoat hang straight. At the LEFT edge Watson's brown tweed shoulder and the brim of his brown bowler stand still and out of focus, nearest the camera and taller than Stamford's head. At the RIGHT edge the brass side-lamp burns on the front corner of the body at Stamford's shoulder height, and past it through the side glass a lit shopfront window and one iron lamp post stand square and soft, with three pedestrians under umbrellas along that pavement. The blank black leather of the folding hood closes across the top of frame above both men.
shots.end: The same place at the front right corner of the box, the same eye height, the same portrait lens across the seat, the same brass side-lamp burning at the RIGHT edge and the same flat grey light, one moment later: Stamford's far arm is out at full stretch across the RIGHT of frame, the elbow locked and the black sleeve foreshortened, his white cuff clear of the wrist and his bare forefinger carried past the brass side-lamp and aimed out through the RIGHT edge of frame at the street; his round clean-shaven face has followed that arm with his chin up and his lips parted on the word; his near hand has come off his knee onto the top of the closed black folding door. At the LEFT edge Watson's brown tweed shoulder and bowler brim hold their place, large and soft. Through the side glass past the pointing hand the lit shopfront window and the iron lamp post that stood square there have travelled out past that edge, and the dark brick face of a warehouse with its arched doorway stands there in their place, two men in dark coats at that doorway. The buttoned leather, the closed folding doors and the black hood across the top of frame hold as they were.
shots.changed: Stamford's arm has reached out to the RIGHT edge of frame, the hand a fist wide.
shots.crowd: three pedestrians under umbrellas along the pavement past the side glass

shots.frame: Wide from across the street: the stone gateway arch of Saint Bartholomew's, the SAME black two-wheeled hansom drawn up at the kerb beneath it, the bay horse's head toward the corner, the cabman up behind the hood; Stamford down on the wet cobbles in his black frock coat, turning in under the arch; Watson in his brown bowler with one boot on the cab step, one hand on the hood's edge, the black stick in his other bare hand reaching for the cobbles; grey light.
shots.motion: Static shot; the hansom stands at the kerb; Watson steps down from the cab step onto the cobbles, plants the stick and limps two steps toward the arch on it over the 2 seconds, while Stamford walks at a normal pace ahead of him in under the arch.
shots.camera: across the street on the far pavement, at the head height of a standing man, a wide lens, the wet cobbles and the near kerb across the bottom of frame and the whole soot-dark brick wall running from the gateway arch at the left of frame to the corner at the right of frame
shots.at_rest: The gateway is one round stone arch standing open in the brick wall at the left of frame, tall enough and wide enough for the hansom to drive straight through it, and its two iron gates stand folded back flat against the brick inside the opening, one leaf to each side, their spear tops level and still. Through that opening the daylight falls on a paved yard, and the worn stone steps rise at the back of the yard to the small side-door, pale and small with distance. The iron railings run from the right-hand jamb of the arch along the pavement to the corner at the right of frame, each spear shorter than the one before it. The same black hansom stands square at the kerb beneath the arch, running on one tall spoked wheel on this near flank and one matching wheel on the far flank, those two the whole of its running gear, their single axle crossing under the middle of the passenger box so the near wheel's top rim stands level with the passengers' shoulders; the two long black shafts run forward from the body to the bay horse, which stands with all four hooves planted on the cobbles and its head toward the corner at the RIGHT of frame, two thirds of a wheel's width of open wet cobble lying between the wheel's front rim and its hind hooves; the brass side-lamp burns at the front corner of the body at shoulder height; the cabman sits on his high seat at the BACK of the roof above and behind the folding hood with the reins slack in his hands. Watson's right boot rests on the cab step with his weight over it, the silver ball knob of the black walking stick under his bare sunburnt right hand and its ferrule held a hand's breadth above the cobbles, his left hand flat on the edge of the folding hood, the brown bowler square on his head. Stamford stands with both boots down on the wet cobbles a stride clear of the wheel, his black frock coat hanging straight, his face toward the opening of the arch. Three men in dark coats stand talking just inside that opening, a porter is halted at the railings with both hands on the shafts of his barrow, and a woman with a basket waits at the far kerb. The light is the flat grey of a wet afternoon and one long wet shine runs along the cobbles from the gutter to the kerb.
shots.crowd: three men in dark coats talking just inside the archway, a porter halted at the railings with both hands on his barrow shafts, and a woman with a basket waiting at the far kerb

shots.frame: Full shot from the foot of the worn stone steps just inside the arch, looking up: Stamford at the top in the open side-door, black frock coat, turned back; Watson seen from behind at the bottom of the flight, both boots together on the lowest step, his weight on the black stick in the bare sunburnt hand on the right of frame, the brown bowler square on his head, the hand on the left of frame hanging at the skirt of his coat.
shots.motion: Static shot; Watson climbs all five steps on his stick, one limping step per second, lifts the bowler off his head as he reaches the top and passes Stamford through the door by 3 seconds; Stamford steps back through the door ahead of him.

cuts.frame: Close on Stamford at the top of the worn stone steps in the open side-door, dark hair, round clean-shaven face, black frock coat, turned back to Watson below him, mouth closed, an uneasy half smile; soot-dark brick behind.
cuts.motion: Static shot; Stamford turns his head from Watson below him to the doorway, pushes the door wide open with his flat hand over 2 seconds, and steps through it, his shoulder leaving the frame by 4 seconds; Watson's bare head and tweed shoulder rise into the bottom of frame behind him by 5 seconds.
cuts.camera: low on the third step looking up at Stamford in the doorway at the top of the flight, a short telephoto lens, his head and shoulders filling the frame against the open black door, the stone door-jamb down the right edge of frame and the lit passage showing narrow past his arm
cuts.at_rest: Stamford stands square on the threshold sill with both feet still, one flat hand laid on the inner face of the open door at the height of his own shoulder, his other hand down at the side of his black frock coat, his round clean-shaven face turned down and back over his shoulder toward Watson below the bottom of frame, his mouth closed on an uneasy half smile, his small bright eyes steady. The door stands open inward, and in the passage past his arm one small yellow gas flame burns in a wall bracket far down that passage. The soot-dark brick of the hospital wall stands to either side of the doorway, streaked by the rain, with one old iron boot-scraper set into the stone at the right edge of frame. The top step is worn hollow and wet under his boots. Far below and behind him at the foot of the wall, three men in dark coats stand talking with their hats on, small and out of focus.
cuts.crowd: three men in dark coats standing far below at the foot of the wall, talking with their hats on

shots.camera: at the foot of the worn stone steps just inside the gateway, set low at the height of the second step and looking up the flight, a normal lens, one folded-back iron gate leaf standing tall at the left edge of frame and the small side-door centred at the top of the flight
shots.at_rest: Both of Watson's boots stand together on the bottom step with his back to the camera, the iron ferrule of the black walking stick set on the stone beside his right boot and the silver ball knob under his bare sunburnt right hand, his left hand hanging at his side by the skirt of his brown tweed coat, the brown bowler square on his head. Five worn stone steps rise ahead of him, each one hollowed in the middle by boots and wet along its edges. Stamford stands at the top of the flight with both feet on the threshold sill of the open side-door, his black frock coat still, one flat hand laid on the inner face of the door, his round clean-shaven face turned down and back toward Watson below him. The side-door stands open inward on a dark passage. The soot-dark brick of the hospital wall rises on both sides of the flight, streaked by the rain. One iron gate leaf stands folded flat against that brick at the left edge of frame, its spear tops level with Watson's shoulder, and the shadow of the archway lies straight across the bottom two steps. Three men in dark coats stand talking at the foot of the wall behind Watson with their backs to him, and a woman with a basket waits out on the far kerb beyond the opening.
shots.end: The same flight of steps from the same low place at the foot of it, the same normal lens and the same grey light. Watson stands at the top of the flight with both boots on the threshold sill and the open doorway standing round him, his back still to the camera and his face in three-quarter turn toward Stamford, the black walking stick planted on the sill under his bare sunburnt right hand, the brown bowler held crown upward at his chest in his bare left hand, his dark hair bare to the grey light. Stamford stands a pace back over the sill inside the dark passage, his black frock coat half taken by that darkness, his round clean-shaven face pale and turned back toward Watson, his flat hand still on the inner face of the door, which now stands wide against the passage wall. The five worn steps below the two men lie empty from the bottom step to the top. The folded-back iron gate leaf holds the left edge of frame with its spear tops level. The shadow of the archway lies across the bottom two steps as it did. The three men in dark coats stand talking at the foot of the wall.
shots.changed: Watson has climbed to the threshold sill at the TOP of frame, a third of its height.
shots.crowd: three men in dark coats talking at the foot of the wall with their backs turned, and a woman with a basket waiting out on the far kerb

shots.frame: Medium shot from behind at the corridor's near end: Stamford a pace ahead in the black frock coat, Watson bareheaded, the brown bowler in the hand on the left of frame, the black stick swinging in the bare hand on the right of frame; bars of window light on the flagstones ahead.
shots.motion: Tracking behind them at Stamford's normal walking pace for the whole shot; Watson limps along on his stick at a normal walking pace while Stamford walks at a normal pace a step ahead of him; both men advance three full strides down the corridor and the bars of window light pass under their boots; Stamford's head turns back over his shoulder to Watson at 2 seconds and forward again.

cuts.frame: Close on Stamford in strict profile walking, a quarter of the way down the corridor, dark hair, round clean-shaven face, mouth closed, eyes ahead; whitewashed wall passing behind.
cuts.motion: Tracking beside him in profile at his normal walking pace for the whole shot; the whitewashed wall and its damp stains stream past behind him as he walks; he turns his head toward Watson beside him at 1.5 seconds and faces ahead again by 3 seconds.
cuts.camera: against the window wall on the RIGHT-hand side of the corridor, level with Stamford's own eyes, a long lens turned a little along the corridor toward its far end, so his head and shoulders in strict profile fill the LEFT two thirds of frame facing the RIGHT edge, the whitewashed wall opposite with its damp stains standing soft behind him, and the low arched passage at the far end showing at the RIGHT edge of frame the height of two thumbnails, a fifteenth of the frame's height
cuts.at_rest: Stamford is caught at the beginning of a stride with his near boot flat on the flagstone below the bottom of frame and his weight rolled over it, his shoulders level and settled and his head held still on them; his round clean-shaven face is in strict profile toward the RIGHT edge of frame with his eyes level down the corridor, his mouth closed, his dark hair parted at the side and lying flat, the collar of the black frock coat square on his shoulders and the dark cravat tied at his throat above the grey waistcoat. Against the whitewashed wall behind him a student in a black coat stands with an open folio held in both hands and his eyes down on the page, and a charwoman kneels at the foot of that wall with a zinc pail standing beside her and both hands flat on a wet cloth on the flagstone. The damp stains and the cold grey daylight lie steady on the wall behind his head.
cuts.crowd: one student in a black coat holding an open folio in both hands at the whitewashed wall, and a charwoman kneeling at its foot with a zinc pail beside her

shots.camera: in the middle of the corridor a stride behind the two men at walking height, a normal lens, square down the corridor, so Watson's brown tweed back fills the LEFT half of frame nearest the camera and Stamford's black frock coat stands a pace ahead of him and smaller in the RIGHT half, the tall barred windows running down the RIGHT side of frame and laying their bars of cold grey daylight across the flagstones, and the low arched passage at the far end of the corridor standing at the CENTRE of frame with its own pale barred window showing inside it, the height of a thumbnail, a thirtieth of the frame's height
shots.at_rest: Both men are caught at the beginning of a stride. Watson's left boot is planted flat on the worn flagstone with his whole weight rolled over it, his right boot at the top of its swing with the heel clear of the stone, the iron ferrule of the black walking stick lifted a hand's breadth above the flagstone under his bare sunburnt right hand at the RIGHT of frame, and the brown bowler hanging by its brim in his other hand at the LEFT of frame with its crown down. Stamford's near boot is flat on the stone with his weight over it and his far boot at the top of its swing, his shoulders level and settled, his dark hair parted at the side, his round clean-shaven face square down the corridor and his eyes straight ahead along it, both his hands loose at his sides. Farther down the corridor two porters in leather aprons stand halted at the LEFT-hand wall with a wheeled trolley between them under a grey cover, each man's hands on its handle, and a nurse in a white cap and long apron stands at a dun-coloured door beyond them with a folded pile of linen held level in both arms. The bars of window light lie still across the flagstones ahead of the two men.
shots.end: The same corridor from the same place a stride behind the two men, the same walking height, the same normal lens and the same cold grey daylight, three strides later: Watson's brown tweed back still fills the LEFT half of frame with his weight down on the black stick planted beside his boot under his bare sunburnt right hand and the brown bowler hanging by its brim in his other hand, one bar of cold window light lying across his shoulders where the bars lay on the flagstones ahead of him; the gap between the two men has opened to two full paces, so Stamford stands smaller in the RIGHT half of frame with his round clean-shaven face turned back over his shoulder to Watson, his chin above his black collar and his eyes on the man behind him; the low arched passage at the far end of the corridor stands at the CENTRE of frame with its pale barred window inside it at a twentieth of the frame's height, larger than it stood; the two porters and their covered trolley stand larger and nearer at the LEFT-hand wall with their hands still on the handle, and the nurse in the white cap and long apron stands at her dun-coloured door beyond them with the linen level in both arms; the tall barred windows hold the RIGHT side of frame and the worn flagstones hold the bottom of it.
shots.changed: Stamford has drawn two paces ahead at the RIGHT of frame, a head shorter than Watson.
shots.crowd: two porters in leather aprons halted at the left-hand wall with a covered wheeled trolley between them, and a nurse in a white cap and long apron at a dun-coloured door beyond them with a folded pile of linen level in both arms

shots.frame: Insert from the corridor, now abreast of the dissecting-room doorway, seen through it: a plain wooden stick lying on a slab beside a body under a grey sheet, cold light from a high window.
shots.motion: Push in through the doorway toward the slab for the whole shot; the stick and the sheet grow from a third of the frame to two thirds and the doorframe passes out of both edges of frame by 3 seconds; a drip runs off the slab's edge to the floor.

cuts.frame: Medium close-up of Watson stopped dead beside the dissecting-room doorway, bareheaded, dark hair swept back, thin moustache, the brown bowler in the hand on the right of frame, the black stick's silver knob under the bare sunburnt hand on the left of frame, staring in, mouth closed, his face grey-white to the lips; Stamford's black shoulder at the edge of frame, nearer the camera, soft.
cuts.motion: Static shot; Watson takes a full step back from the doorway on his stick, his whole body moving to the right of frame, over the first 1.5 seconds; then his head and shoulders turn round to Stamford at the frame edge by 3 seconds; his lips stay closed.
cuts.camera: in the middle of the corridor a half pace on the near-end side of the dissecting-room doorway, level with Watson's own eyes, a short telephoto lens, so the dark jamb of that doorway stands down the LEFT edge of frame nearest the camera, Watson's head and shoulders fill the CENTRE of frame in three-quarter face turned toward that jamb, and the black frock-coated shoulder of Stamford stands large and soft at the BOTTOM RIGHT corner of frame nearest the camera
cuts.at_rest: Watson stands stopped dead with both boots flat on the flagstone and his whole weight carried over the silver ball knob of the black walking stick under his bare sunburnt right hand at the LEFT of frame, the iron ferrule set square on the stone; the brown bowler is held by its brim in his other hand at the RIGHT of frame with the crown toward the camera; his dark hair is swept back and bare to the grey light, his thin waxed moustache lies level, his lips are closed and his face is grey-white to them, and his eyes are fixed on the opening at the LEFT edge of frame; Stamford's black shoulder is settled and still at the BOTTOM RIGHT corner. Behind Watson the tall barred windows run away down the RIGHT of frame and lay their bars of daylight along the flagstones, and in that light two students in black coats stand at a dun-coloured door with one open folio held between them and a charwoman stands at the whitewashed wall with both hands on the handle of her zinc pail.
cuts.end: The same stretch of corridor beside the same dissecting-room doorway, the same eye height, the same short telephoto lens and the same cold grey daylight, one step later: Watson stands a full pace to the RIGHT of frame from where he stood and smaller in it, both boots flat on the flagstone again with the black stick planted on the stone before them under his bare sunburnt right hand and the brown bowler still held by its brim in his other hand; his head and shoulders have come round to the BOTTOM RIGHT corner of frame, his face turned there and his eyes on Stamford's black frock coat, his lips closed and his colour still grey-white; the dark jamb of the doorway stands down the LEFT edge of frame with the flagstone at its foot lying empty where his boots were; behind him the tall barred windows and their bars of daylight hold the RIGHT of frame, the two students hold their dun-coloured door with the open folio between them, and the charwoman stands at the whitewashed wall with both hands on the handle of her zinc pail.
cuts.changed: Watson has stepped a pace to the RIGHT of frame and stands a head smaller.
cuts.crowd: two students in black coats at a dun-coloured door with one open folio between them, and a charwoman at the whitewashed wall with both hands on her zinc pail

shots.camera: in the middle of the corridor abreast of the dissecting-room doorway, at walking height, a normal lens, turned square into the opening, so the dark jambs of that doorway stand down BOTH edges of frame, the slab lies across the middle of frame at a third of its height with the grey sheet over the body on it, and the high barred window stands pale at the TOP of frame above the slab
shots.at_rest: The plain wooden stick lies along the near edge of the slab with its whole length flat on the wood and its turned ball end at the CENTRE of frame; the grey sheet lies over the body in settled folds with its hem hanging down the slab's near side; one bead of water hangs swelling under the slab's edge at the RIGHT of the stick, holding to the wet wood, and a wide dark wet patch lies already on the flagstone below it; the cold light from the high window lies flat and even along the sheet and the scarred wood. At the back wall under that window a mortuary porter in a leather apron stands at a stone sink with both hands down in the water and his back to the room, and a second porter stands beside him with a folded canvas over his arm.
shots.end: The same dissecting room through the same opening in the same flat cold light, one moment later: the dark jambs have passed out of both edges of frame, the slab and the grey sheet fill two thirds of the frame's height with the scars in the wood and the folds of the sheet large and sharp, and the plain wooden stick's turned ball end stands at the CENTRE of frame the size of a fist; the bead has fallen and lies as a dark coin of water on the flagstone below the slab's edge, with a second bead swelling under the wood where the first one hung; the high barred window stands larger and paler at the TOP of frame; the mortuary porter at the stone sink stands where he stood with his hands in the water, his shoulders at the LEFT edge of frame, and the second porter stands beside him with the folded canvas over his arm.
shots.changed: The slab has grown to fill the CENTRE of frame at two thirds of its height.

shots.frame: Full shot from behind, low on the flagstones at the corridor's far end: Stamford through the low arched passage holding its door open, Watson's back nearer the camera, bareheaded, the brown bowler in the hand on the left of frame, the black stick planted under the bare hand on the right of frame, weight on the stick.
shots.motion: Static shot; Watson limps along on his stick at a normal walking pace down the corridor toward the passage, two full strides over the 2.8 seconds, growing smaller in frame; Stamford stands in the open doorway at the far end with his hand on the door.

cuts.frame: Insert low at the corridor's far end, from behind: Watson's boot on the worn flagstone with the black stick's ferrule planted beside it, a bar of window light across them; ahead, the threshold of the low arched passage and the held door.
cuts.motion: Static shot low on the flagstones; the boot lifts, swings forward through a full stride and lands a step nearer the passage by 1.5 seconds; the stick's ferrule lifts and plants beside it by 2.5 seconds; the bar of window light passes over them.
cuts.camera: set down on the flagstones at the corridor's far end a half pace behind Watson's boots, a hand's breadth above the stone and level with it, a close-focus lens looking along the floor toward the low arched passage, so the boot and the stick's iron ferrule stand large across the BOTTOM LEFT of frame, the worn flagstones run away up the middle of it, the dark held door stands at the RIGHT edge, and the arched threshold at the far end stands at the CENTRE RIGHT of frame at a quarter of the frame's height
cuts.at_rest: The near boot stands on the worn flagstone at the LEFT of frame with the weight rolled forward onto its toe and its heel a hair clear of the stone, the ankle bent and the trouser leg hanging straight over the boot's counter; the black walking stick stands plumb at the CENTRE of frame with its iron ferrule set square on the stone and the hem of the brown tweed coat above it; one bar of cold window light lies still across the boot and the ferrule and along the wet flagstones beyond them, and the water standing in the hollows of the stone holds steady. At the RIGHT of frame a charwoman's zinc pail stands on the flagstones with a wet cloth folded over its rim and the grey hem of her skirt beside it, and farther along at the LEFT a porter's boots stand halted beside the wheels of a covered trolley.

shots.camera: in the middle of the corridor at its far end, set low at the height of a man's knee and looking along the flagstones, a wide lens, so the worn flagstones and their bars of daylight fill the BOTTOM half of frame, Watson's brown tweed back stands in the LEFT half at half the frame's height seen from below, the tall barred windows run down the RIGHT side of frame, and the low arched passage closes the CENTRE of frame at the height of a hand with its open door swung back at the RIGHT of the opening, Stamford standing in it and the pale barred window of the far wall inside the arch
shots.at_rest: Watson is caught at the beginning of a stride with his left boot planted flat on the worn flagstone and his weight rolled over it and over the silver ball knob of the black walking stick under his bare sunburnt right hand at the RIGHT of his back, the iron ferrule lifted a hand's breadth above the stone, his right boot at the top of its swing with the heel clear of it, the brown bowler hanging by its brim in his other hand at the LEFT of frame and his dark hair bare above his collar. Stamford stands square on the threshold of the low arched passage with both boots down on the stone, one flat hand laid on the edge of the open door at the height of his own shoulder, his other hand loose at his side and his round clean-shaven face turned back along the corridor toward Watson. The bars of cold daylight lie still across the flagstones between the two men. cuts.end: the same open doorway at the near end of the room, the same normal lens looking back along the aisle and the same cold grey light, one action later: the two men have come three paces up the aisle and now stand close to the camera, filling the frame from the bottom edge to the top, both of them from the knees up; Watson is at the LEFT of frame, his gaunt sunburnt face, dark swept-back hair and thin waxed moustache large and sharp, his weight down over the silver ball knob under his bare sunburnt right hand with the black stick's ferrule planted on the boards at the bottom left of frame, the brown bowler still crown upward at his chest in his left hand; Stamford is at the RIGHT of frame, his black frock coat filling that side and his round clean-shaven face turned a little toward Watson; the long benches have opened out past both side edges of frame; the aisle behind the two men shows as one narrow slot between their shoulders, the tall arched window keeping its own small size high at the centre with Holmes bent over his table under it; the near Bunsen lamp burns at the bottom right corner and the student at the far bench holds his flask to the light
cuts.changed: The two men have come three paces up the aisle and fill the frame from the knees.
cuts.crowd: one student in shirtsleeves at a far bench holding a flask up to the daylight

shots.camera: across the bench at its near edge, set at the height of the two joined hands and a foot from them, a short telephoto lens, the clasp filling the MIDDLE of frame with the bottle-green velvet cuff running out to the LEFT edge and the brown tweed cuff running out to the RIGHT edge, and the tall arched window standing pale and soft across the whole TOP of frame behind them
shots.at_rest: Two hands are in this frame and they are these two: from the bottle-green velvet cuff at the LEFT edge, its white shirt cuff turned back at the wrist, comes Holmes's right hand, pale indoor skin; from the brown tweed cuff at the RIGHT edge, its white linen cuff showing, comes Watson's bare sunburnt right hand, brown as a nut. One cuff at each edge, one wrist in each cuff, one hand on each wrist, and these two hands are the whole of the flesh in frame. The two palms are shut together in one plain grip at the centre of frame with each thumb laid flat over the back of the other man's hand, the two forearms level and steady and both wrists quiet; the small white plaster is wound twice round Holmes's forefinger where that finger lies across the back of Watson's sunburnt hand, turned out to the camera and lit by the window; the grip is closed and at rest; the bench top, the ranked bottles and the pale window stand soft and out of focus behind them.
shots.end: the same place across the bench at the same height, the same short telephoto lens, the same pale window across the top of frame and the same two cuffs at the two edges, one action later: the grip has opened and the two hands stand a hand's width apart at the centre of frame, the fingers of each still half curled from the clasp; Holmes's right hand is at the LEFT of frame, drawing back toward the bottle-green velvet cuff, its pale forefinger straight with the small white plaster wound round it turned to the camera; Watson's bare sunburnt right hand is at the RIGHT of frame, opening toward the brown tweed cuff with its palm turned inward; these two hands are still the whole of the flesh in frame, one at each side; the bench top, the ranked bottles and the pale window stand soft behind them
shots.changed: The grip has opened and the two hands stand a hand's width apart at the CENTRE.

shots.frame: Medium close-up of Watson stopped on the wet pavement just outside the gateway arch, brown bowler on, dark hair, thin moustache, turned to Stamford off frame, the question on his face, lips just closed; the silver knob of the black stick under his bare sunburnt hand at the bottom of frame; iron railings and the hospital wall behind him.
shots.motion: Static shot; Watson speaks the line to the man beside him off frame; as he speaks he turns his whole upper body round toward Stamford's side, the bowler brim turning with him, over 2 seconds; after the line he raises the stick and points it back at the arch behind his right shoulder by 4.5 seconds.
shots.camera: out on the pavement an arm's length from Watson and level with his own eyes, a portrait lens, his head and shoulders filling the frame in three-quarter turn toward the left edge, the round stone of the gateway arch standing whole and soft behind his right shoulder
shots.at_rest: Watson stands stopped with both boots planted square on the pavement flags, the iron ferrule of the black walking stick set on the stone before his right boot and the silver ball knob under his bare sunburnt right hand at the bottom of frame, the brown bowler square on his head with his dark hair and thin waxed moustache under its brim, his face turned toward the left edge of frame, the question standing in his eyes and his lips just closed. Behind his right shoulder the gateway arch stands whole in the soot-dark brick, its two iron gates folded back flat inside the opening and the pale worn steps showing small through it. Behind his left shoulder the iron railings run away along the pavement toward the corner, each spear shorter than the one before. The low sun lays one band of amber along the top course of the hospital wall and leaves the pavement flags in blue shade. A woman with a basket stands still at the far kerb with her hands on the handle, and a porter has set his barrow down against the railings and stands beside it.
shots.crowd: a woman with a basket standing still at the far kerb with her hands on the handle, and a porter standing beside his barrow set down at the railings

shots.frame: Medium two-shot side on along the railings, halfway to the corner, both walking: Stamford nearer the camera in strict profile, dark hair, round clean-shaven face, black frock coat, a half smile, mouth closed; Watson beyond him, brown bowler on, watching his face, the black stick's silver knob swinging in his bare sunburnt hand on the camera side.
shots.motion: Tracking beside them at Stamford's normal walking pace for the whole shot; Watson limps along on his stick at a normal walking pace while Stamford walks at a normal pace beside him, shortening his stride to Watson's; the railings and the hospital wall stream past behind them; Stamford shrugs both shoulders high and drops them at 1.5 seconds and turns his head to Watson.

cuts.frame: Close on Watson walking along the railings, brown bowler on, thin moustache, his eyes on Stamford beside him at the frame edge, mouth closed; the hospital wall and railings sliding past behind him.
cuts.motion: Tracking ahead of him at his limping pace for the whole shot; the railings stream past behind him; Watson's head turns from Stamford beside him to the street ahead and back over 2 seconds; at 3 seconds he stops dead on his stick and Stamford's black shoulder passes on out of frame ahead of him.
cuts.camera: out on the street side of the railings a few paces ahead of the two men and angled back along the pavement, level with Watson's eyes, a portrait lens, Watson's head and shoulders filling the left of frame in three-quarter front view and the shoulder of Stamford's black frock coat dark and soft at the right edge
cuts.at_rest: Watson is caught on the stride with his left boot planted flat on the flags and his weight carried over the black walking stick, the silver ball knob under his bare sunburnt right hand just inside the bottom right of frame, his right boot at the top of its swing. The brown bowler sits square on his head with his dark hair and thin waxed moustache under its brim, his mouth closed, his eyes turned to Stamford at the right edge of frame. Behind his shoulder the iron railings run back along the pavement, each spear shorter than the one before, to the gateway arch standing small and soft in the soot-dark wall with its two gate leaves folded back flat inside the opening. The band of low amber sun lies along the top course of that wall and the pavement holds blue shade. A porter stands halted at the railings halfway back with his barrow shafts down on the flags, and two women with baskets stand talking at the far kerb.

shots.camera: out on the street side of the railings, level with the two men at their chest height, a normal lens, Stamford in strict profile nearest the camera at the right of frame and Watson a half pace behind him at the left of frame, both of them from the knees up, the pavement flags and the railings running back to the arch at the far left of frame
shots.at_rest: Both men are caught on the stride, each with his near boot planted flat on the flags and his far boot at the top of its swing with the heel clear of the stone. Watson's black walking stick is planted on the flags at the left of frame with his weight carried over the silver ball knob under his bare sunburnt right hand, that shoulder dropped low on it, the brown bowler square on his head and his eyes on Stamford's face. Stamford's shoulders are down and level, both his hands at his sides, his black frock coat hanging straight, his mouth closed on a half smile, his face set straight ahead along the pavement. The iron railings run past the two men at waist height from the right edge of frame back toward the left, each spear shorter than the one before, and at the far left the gateway arch stands in the soot-dark wall with its two gate leaves folded back flat inside the opening. The hospital wall carries one band of low amber sun along its top course and the pavement below lies in blue shade. A porter stands halted at the railings behind them with both hands on his barrow shafts, and a woman with a basket waits at the corner ahead.
